# **Technical and Business Architecture**

## **Progressive SaaS Platform for Domain Name Management and Acquisition**

## **Systemic Market Evolution and Modern Domaining Challenges**

The domain name industry is experiencing a structural shift, driven by the emergence of high-value artificial intelligence ventures requiring premium extensions, and the expanding intersection between Web2 ICANN-regulated namespaces and decentralized Web3 cryptographic identities.1 Historically, domain portfolios have been managed using fragmented tools, with independent domain investors, brokers, and agencies relying on a combination of localized spreadsheets, disparate auction platforms, and manual outbound email outreach.1 This fragmentation introduces operational bottlenecks, particularly in tracking acquisition return on investment, monitoring expirations across different registrar dashboards, and executing outreach campaigns to secure end-user buyers.1

To solve these inefficiencies, contemporary platforms must transition from static registries into active, intelligence-driven command centers. This involves moving beyond basic portfolio listing tools and implementing features such as automated valuation modeling, outbound lead generation, and programmatic DNS routing.1 Furthermore, the industry is transitioning from human-reliant web interfaces to machine-to-machine integrations.2 This shift is exemplified by the release of Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers and dedicated APIs by major registrars such as Cloudflare, NameSilo, and Name.com, which allow artificial intelligence agents to search, purchase, and configure domains autonomously.2 In tandem, registries are developing protocols like GoDaddy's Agent Name Service (ANS) to assign cryptographically verifiable digital identities to automated agents, establishing a secure framework for the future of agentic internet transactions.5

## **Website API and Scraping Integration Analysis**

Building a unified domain intelligence platform requires integrating with multiple registrars, auction houses, and expired domain aggregators. Because these platforms vary widely in API availability, access requirements, and data structures, the system must utilize a hybrid integration strategy. Some platforms provide robust RESTful interfaces or Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers, while others require advanced scraping, normalization, and deduplication pipelines to extract clean, actionable data.  
The following comparative matrix outlines the technical parameters, costs, and integration strategies for the ten primary target websites:

| Website URL | Platform Category | API Status | Access Requirements / Costs | Data Extraction, Filtering, and Deduping Strategy |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **Dynadot** (dynadot.com) 6 | Registrar & Aftermarket | Has API 6 | Free with registered account; rate limits depend on pricing tier.6 | Query API for aftermarket listings, expired auctions, and closeouts.6 Parse JSON responses, filter by TLD, and deduplicate against existing portfolio records. |
| **GoDaddy** (godaddy.com) 7 | Registrar & Aftermarket | Has API 7 | 1+ domain in account for DNS/Management 7; 50+ domains for Availability API.7 Rate limits: 60 req/sec, 20,000 req/month.8 | Programmatic DNS updates and nameserver management via REST API.8 Parse registration data, filter out duplicate marketplace listings, and normalize WHOIS fields.8 |
| **Namecheap** (namecheap.com) 9 | Registrar | Has API 9 | Requires 20+ domains, $50 account balance, OR $50 spent in past 2 years.9 | Pull registered domains and DNS configurations.1 Normalize domain expiration dates to ISO 8601 format and clean registrant contact structures. |
| **ExpiredDomains** (expireddomains.net) 10 | Expired Domain Aggregator | No API 10 | Web access is free; programmatic access requires web scraping.10 | Deploy headless browsers via scraping APIs to extract pending-delete and auction lists.10 Strip HTML, filter by SEO metrics (backlinks, domain age), and deduplicate by domain name string.10 |
| **NameGulf** (namegulf.com) | Aftermarket Brokerage | No API | Public web interface; scraping required. | Scrape listed domain names, categories, and asking prices. Deduplicate against global aftermarket databases using canonical domain name matching. |
| **DropCatch** (dropcatch.com) | Drop-Catching Service | No API | Public drop lists; scraping required. | Scrape daily pending-delete auction catalogs. Parse ASCII text tables, clean whitespace, extract key bidding indicators, and merge with active backorder queues. |
| **NameJet** (namejet.com) 12 | Domain Auctions | Restricted API 12 | Partner API requires reseller agreement 12; otherwise scraping is required. | Execute scraping scripts against active auction directories. Extract current high bids, bidding histories, and end times; filter out junk domains based on keyword patterns. |
| **Porkbun** (porkbun.com) 13 | Registrar | Has API 14 | Free; included with any registrar account.14 | Use REST endpoints to fetch TLD pricing, execute DNS CRUD operations, and retrieve Let's Encrypt SSL certificates.15 Format pricing outputs to unify multi-currency ledger fields. |
| **DomainEasy** (domaineasy.com) | Registrar & Aftermarket | No API | Public web interface; scraping required. | Scrape domain availability checks and marketplace listings. Parse, sanitize, and validate domain strings, and remove duplicate records from the local indexing cache. |
| **Cloudflare** (cloudflare.com) 2 | Registrar & DNS | Has API 2 | Free; domains offered at-cost without markup.2 | Integrate Cloudflare Registrar API to query real-time availability and execute registrations.2 Parse JSON responses and synchronize DNS records using native MCP servers.2 |

### **Sourcing, Filtering, and Deduping Pipeline Architecture**

To construct a unified, high-integrity domain database, the platform must process raw data streams through a structured extraction, transformation, and loading (ETL) pipeline. This pipeline converts messy, unstructured inputs into standardized database records, preventing duplicate entries and filtering out low-value domain spam.

\+-------------------------------------------------------------+  
|                     DATA INGESTION LAYER                     |  
|  \- REST APIs (GoDaddy, Porkbun, Cloudflare, NameSilo)       |  
|  \- Scraping APIs (ExpiredDomains, DropCatch, NameGulf)     |  
\+------------------------------+------------------------------+  
                               |  
                               v  
\+-------------------------------------------------------------+  
|                   PRE-PROCESSING & CLEANING                 |  
|  \- Convert domain names to lowercase ASCII (punycode)       |  
|  \- Strip subdomains and protocol prefixes (http, https, www)|  
|  \- Parse and normalize expiration dates to ISO 8601 format   |  
\+------------------------------+------------------------------+  
                               |  
                               v  
\+-------------------------------------------------------------+  
|                  FILTERING & TRADEMARK CHECK                |  
|  \- Apply regex filters to remove character-spam domains     |  
|  \- Cross-reference with open-access trademark registries     |  
|  \- Drop domains with historical spam flags (pharma, adult)  |  
\+------------------------------+------------------------------+  
                               |  
                               v  
\+-------------------------------------------------------------+  
|                     DEDUPLICATION ENGINE                    |  
|  \- Resolve duplicate listings across multiple marketplaces  |  
|  \- Merge overlapping auction data into a single entity       |  
|  \- Prioritize the listing with the lowest transactional fee  |  
\+------------------------------+------------------------------+  
                               |  
                               v  
\+-------------------------------------------------------------+  
|                     TARGET STORAGE LAYER                    |  
|  \- Version v0: Localized SQLite or single-node PostgreSQL   |  
|  \- Version v1+: Cloud PostgreSQL with Redis cache layer     |  
\+-------------------------------------------------------------+

#### **Step 1: Pre-Processing and String Cleaning**

When ingesting data from scraping targets such as ExpiredDomains.net or DropCatch, the pipeline first normalizes the raw text strings. It converts all domain names to lowercase ASCII characters and strips protocol prefixes (e.g., http://, https://, www.). If the domain contains non-ASCII characters, the engine encodes it into Punycode (e.g., converting münchen.com to xn--mnchen-3ya.com) to prevent database indexing errors. It then parses dates of various formats (e.g., "Dec 12, 2026", "2026/12/12", "12-12-2026") and converts them into standardized ISO 8601 UTC timestamps (YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS).

#### **Step 2: Content Filtering and Spam Suppression**

To maintain high database quality, the platform applies several programmatic filters to incoming domain records:

* **Syntax Filtering**: Removes domains with excessive hyphens (e.g., containing more than two consecutive hyphens) or suspicious character distributions.  
* **Trademark Verification**: Cross-references parsed keywords with open-access trademark databases to flag and filter out potential typosquatting or brand infringements, mitigating legal risks under the Uniform Domain-Name Dispute-Resolution Policy (UDRP).1  
* **SEO Sanitization**: When ingesting expired domain data, the pipeline filters out domains with historical search engine spam flags (e.g., domains previously used for black-hat SEO, pharmaceutical spam, or adult content distribution) by checking external reputation lists and search engine indexes.1

#### **Step 3: Multi-Marketplace Deduplication**

Domain sellers frequently list their assets on multiple aftermarket platforms simultaneously to maximize exposure (e.g., listing a domain on GoDaddy Aftermarket, NameJet, and NameGulf at the same time).1 To prevent duplicate listings from cluttering the platform's database, the deduplication engine applies a strict hashing and grouping algorithm:

* **Canonical Resolution**: The engine groups duplicate records by their canonical domain name.  
* **Listing Consolidation**: It merges overlapping marketplace and auction data into a single domain entity, creating a unified dashboard view.  
* **Fee Optimization**: If the same domain is listed at different price points or on different marketplaces, the system highlights the listing with the lowest transactional fee, ensuring maximum value for the buyer.1

## **Progressive Technical Architecture and Development Roadmap**

To manage development costs and maintain financial control, the platform is designed to evolve progressively across three distinct software versions. This roadmap scales the platform's infrastructure and functional capabilities as the business grows.

\+-------------------------------------------------------------+  
|                         VERSION v0                          |  
|  \- Deployment: Local Single-Instance / Lightweight Docker   |  
|  \- Storage: Localized SQLite Database File                  |  
|  \- Core Functions: Directory, P\&L, Prospecting, Basic AI    |  
|  \- APIs: Free rate-limited public RDAP / WHOIS lookups      |  
\+------------------------------+------------------------------+  
                               |  
                               v  
\+-------------------------------------------------------------+  
|                         VERSION v1                          |  
|  \- Deployment: Cloud Multi-Tenant SaaS (AWS/Hetzner)        |  
|  \- Storage: Cloud PostgreSQL Database with Redis Cache      |  
|  \- Core Functions: Trello-style Outbound CRM, Notifications  |  
|  \- APIs: Direct Registrar Sync, NameBio Comparative Engine  |  
\+------------------------------+------------------------------+  
                               |  
                               v  
\+-------------------------------------------------------------+  
|                         VERSION v3                          |  
|  \- Deployment: Enterprise Microservices with Kubernetes     |  
|  \- Storage: Distributed PostgreSQL, Kafka Event Streaming  |  
|  \- Core Functions: Recursive Agent Trading, White-Label Pages|  
|  \- APIs: Stripe, Escrow.com, Developer APIs, Webhooks      |  
\+-------------------------------------------------------------+

### **Version v0: Single-Instance CRM & Portfolio Ledger**

* **Deployment Architecture**: Local single-instance deployment packaged in a lightweight Docker container.17 This architecture is designed to run on minimal infrastructure, such as a basic virtual private server (VPS) or a local development machine, requiring no complex cloud orchestration.19  
* **Database Engine**: A local SQLite database or a single-node PostgreSQL database.17  
* **Functional Limits**:  
  * *Domain Management*: Supports manual domain entry and bulk CSV imports.1 It uses free public RDAP and rate-limited WHOIS endpoints to monitor nameservers, registration dates, and SSL expirations.18  
  * *Profit/Loss Ledger*: Tracks initial purchase prices, annual renewal costs, and holding times.1  
  * *Prospect Finder*: Parses domain keywords and queries public RDAP registries to identify companies using alternative TLDs (e.g., finding the .net or .org owners of a user's .com domain).1  
  * *Basic AI Agent*: Generates simple outbound sales pitches using the user's personal, rate-limited OpenAI/Anthropic API key.1  
  * *User Access*: Features a localized three-tier account system (Free, Premium, Enterprise) with rate-limiting enforced at the application layer. No integrated payment gateways or cryptographic operations are present in this version.

### **Version v1: Cloud-Native SaaS with Predictive Valuation**

* **Deployment Architecture**: Multi-tenant cloud-native SaaS hosted on high-availability cloud infrastructure (e.g., Hetzner, AWS).21  
* **Database Engine**: Cloud-hosted PostgreSQL with a Redis caching layer to handle high read/write traffic.  
* **Functional Limits**:  
  * *Registrar Integrations*: Automatically synchronizes domains, DNS records, and renewal costs using direct API integrations with GoDaddy, Namecheap, Porkbun, and NameSilo.3  
  * *Outbound CRM*: Features an interactive, Kanban-style negotiation pipeline (similar to Trello or HubSpot) to manage active leads, offers, and counter-offers.1  
  * *Advanced Scraping Pipelines*: Integrates with proxy-rotating services like ScrapingBee or Apify to scrape expired domain data and SEO metrics from ExpiredDomains.net.10  
  * *Predictive Valuation*: Features a comparative engine that cross-references domain attributes with historical sales data from the NameBio API to flag undervalued assets.1  
  * *Transactional Alerts*: Runs automated email notification services to alert users of upcoming expirations or new negotiation updates.1

### **Version v3: Enterprise Brokerage & Autonomous Agent Trading**

* **Deployment Architecture**: Distributed microservices architecture managed with Kubernetes, using Apache Kafka for high-throughput event streaming.1  
* **Database Engine**: Horizontally scaled PostgreSQL cluster combined with a distributed Redis cache.  
* **Functional Limits**:  
  * *Autonomous AI Agents*: Recursive AI agents that analyze market trends, find undervalued domains, submit auction bids, and negotiate sales autonomously via registrar MCP servers.1  
  * *White-Label Landing Pages*: Automatically generates fast, SEO-optimized "For Sale" landing pages with built-in negotiation chatbots and dynamic payment calculators.1  
  * *Payment Gateway Integration*: Facilitates direct domain transfers and secure payouts using Stripe Connect and Escrow.com APIs.1  
  * *Developer Ecosystem*: Provides public developer APIs, webhooks, and software development kits (SDKs) to enable high-volume programmatic management.1  
  * *DeFi Domain Lending*: Integrates decentralized finance protocols, allowing users to lock high-value domains into smart contracts as collateral for stablecoin loans.1

## **Product Requirement Document (PRD) for the Version v0 MVP**

### **1\. Functional Specifications**

#### **1.1 Domain Directory, Listing, and Management**

* **Manual Entry & Bulk Import**: Users can add domains individually or upload entire portfolios via standard CSV files.1  
* **Custom Data Tracking**: Supports custom fields for each domain record, enabling users to track notes, associated projects, and registrar account identifiers.18  
* **DNS & Nameserver Verification**: Background workers query public DNS servers to verify nameserver configurations and check the expiration status of active SSL certificates.18  
* **Segment Filtering**: Users can filter and segment their portfolios by TLD, registrar, or custom tags.18

#### **1.2 Profit/Loss Ledger**

* **Cost Tracking**: Tracks individual domain acquisition costs, annual renewal fees, and any secondary holding expenses.1  
* **Tenure Tracking**: Automatically calculates the exact holding period of each domain, tracking amortized costs in real-time.1  
* **Multi-Currency Support**: Users can choose their preferred local currency, and the system handles exchange rates using free public conversion APIs.18

#### **1.3 Prospect Finder**

* **Keyword Parser**: Automatically parses domain names into keywords (e.g., parsing austintechsolutions.com into Austin, Tech, and Solutions).  
* **Alternative Extension Checker**: Checks the registration status of the parsed keywords across other standard extensions, such as .net, .org, .co, and .io.1  
* **Public RDAP Inquiries**: Queries free, rate-limited public RDAP endpoints to check if alternative extensions are active and retrieve basic registration metadata.20  
* **Lead Identification**: Flags active sites on alternative extensions as potential buyers who might want to purchase the premium .com version of the domain.1

#### **1.4 Basic AI Agent**

* **Rate-Limited Generation**: Includes a prompt-generation engine that interfaces with standard LLMs using the user's personal, rate-limited OpenAI or Anthropic API key.1  
* **Outreach Drafting**: Generates personalized outbound email pitches targeting the prospective buyers identified by the Prospect Finder.1  
* **Execution Controls**: Imposes strict rate limits (e.g., maximum 5 AI operations per hour on free accounts) to prevent API key abuse and control execution costs.

#### **1.5 Three-Tier Access Management**

To prepare the platform for future SaaS monetization, the local database enforces a three-tier access model (Free, Premium, Enterprise). This system restricts feature access and API routing based on the user's tier assignment:

| Feature Specification | Free Tier | Premium Tier | Enterprise Tier |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **Max Domain Inventory** | Up to 10 domains | Up to 1,000 domains | Unlimited domain entries |
| **Outreach Email Drafting** | Manual copy-paste only | Integrated drafting; direct SMTP setup | Dynamic templates with CRM synchronization 1 |
| **RDAP/WHOIS Queries** | 5 direct lookups per day 20 | 100 automated lookups per day 20 | High-frequency API integration 20 |
| **API Support** | Single free public endpoint | Multi-registrar integrations 3 | Full REST API access & webhooks 1 |
| **Task Automation** | Manual trigger only | Automated cron task runner 19 | Continuous queue processing 19 |
| **Financial Ledger** | Basic manual entry | Automated cost synchronization 1 | Multi-currency export & custom ledger categories 18 |
| **Support Level** | Documentation & self-serve | Email ticket support | One-on-one integration SLAs 1 |

\+---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+  
|                                 USER WORKFLOW: OUTBOUND PROSPECTING                               |  
\+---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+  
                                                                                                      
 \[User\] \--- 1\. Submits CSV of Domains \---\> \[Portfolio Ledger Engine\] \--- 2\. Persists to DB \----+      
                                                                                               |      
                                                                                               v      
 \[User\] \<--- 5\. Displays Leads Table \<----- \[Prospect Finder\] \<--- 3\. Parses & Extracts \-------+      
    |                                              |                                                  
    | (Selects Lead & Clicks "Draft")              | 4\. Queries Rate-Limited RDAP APIs                
    v                                              v                                                  
 \--- 6\. Formulates Prompt \-------------------\> \[External LLM API (User Key)\]         
        ^                                                                  |                          
        |                                                                  v                          
        \+-------- 7\. Returns Personalized Outreach Email Draft \------------+                        

#### **Workflow 1: Outbound Prospecting Campaign**

1. **Ingestion**: The user uploads a CSV file containing their domain portfolio. The Portfolio Ledger Engine parses the file and saves the domain records to the database.1  
2. **Analysis**: The user selects a specific domain (e.g., quantumdev.com) and clicks "Find Prospects".1  
3. **Extraction**: The Prospect Finder parses the domain name into keywords, checks alternative extensions (e.g., quantumdev.net, quantumdev.org), and queries public RDAP registries to check their registration status.1  
4. **Reporting**: The system displays a table of active alternative domains, flagging the businesses using those domains as potential sales leads.1  
5. **Drafting**: The user selects a target lead and clicks "Generate Outreach Draft".1  
6. **Generation**: The Basic AI Agent formulates a custom prompt containing the domain details and lead metadata, and sends it to the external LLM API using the user's personal API key.1  
7. **Review**: The generated email draft is displayed on screen, allowing the user to copy, edit, or save the message.

#### **Workflow 2: Financial Reconciliation and Audit**

1. **Data Ingestion**: The user manually inputs or imports a domain's acquisition cost and purchase date.  
2. **Ledger Update**: The system updates the transaction ledger, creating an audit trail of all expenses.1  
3. **Cost Amortization**: A background worker calculates the exact holding period and computes the total holding cost by adding historical renewal fees to the initial purchase price.1  
4. **Financial Dashboard**: The dashboard displays the amortized cost, active renewal rates, and estimated portfolio burn rate, helping the user evaluate the financial health of their assets.1

### **3\. Database Schema Design (SQLite-Compatible)**

To ensure ease of deployment and platform portability, the v0 database is designed using an SQLite-compatible relational schema.17 The tables below outline the structural SQL definitions:

SQL  
\-- Table: users  
CREATE TABLE users (  
    id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,  
    email VARCHAR(255) UNIQUE NOT NULL,  
    password\_hash VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,  
    tier VARCHAR(50) CHECK(tier IN ('free', 'premium', 'enterprise')) NOT NULL DEFAULT 'free',  
    created\_at TIMESTAMP DEFAULT CURRENT\_TIMESTAMP  
);

\-- Table: domains  
CREATE TABLE domains (  
    id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,  
    user\_id INTEGER NOT NULL,  
    domain\_name VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,  
    registrar VARCHAR(100) NOT NULL,  
    acquisition\_date DATE NOT NULL,  
    expiry\_date DATE NOT NULL,  
    acquisition\_cost DECIMAL(10,2) NOT NULL DEFAULT 0.00,  
    renewal\_cost DECIMAL(10,2) NOT NULL DEFAULT 0.00,  
    nameservers TEXT NULL,  
    status VARCHAR(50) DEFAULT 'active',  
    FOREIGN KEY (user\_id) REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE  
);

\-- Table: ledger  
CREATE TABLE ledger (  
    id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,  
    domain\_id INTEGER NOT NULL,  
    transaction\_type VARCHAR(50) NOT NULL,  
    amount DECIMAL(10,2) NOT NULL,  
    transaction\_date DATE NOT NULL,  
    notes TEXT NULL,  
    FOREIGN KEY (domain\_id) REFERENCES domains(id) ON DELETE CASCADE  
);

\-- Table: prospects  
CREATE TABLE prospects (  
    id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,  
    domain\_id INTEGER NOT NULL,  
    prospect\_domain VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,  
    company\_name VARCHAR(255) NULL,  
    contact\_email VARCHAR(255) NULL,  
    outreach\_status VARCHAR(50) DEFAULT 'uncontacted',  
    last\_contact\_date DATE NULL,  
    FOREIGN KEY (domain\_id) REFERENCES domains(id) ON DELETE CASCADE  
);

### **4\. Non-Functional Requirements**

#### **4.1 Local Security & Key Protection**

* **Password Encryption**: User passwords must be hashed using strong, standard hashing algorithms (such as Argon2id or bcrypt) before storage.  
* **Credential Handling**: To protect user security, the platform does not store registrar account passwords or master API keys in the database.19 Any user-supplied API keys must be encrypted in transit and held in memory only when active, preventing permanent exposure.19  
* **Access Controls**: The application forces secure HTTPS connections and supports basic HTTP authentication as an optional security layer for self-hosted instances.19

#### **4.2 Crawler Exclusions & Search Privacy**

* **Robots Policy**: To prevent search engines from crawling and indexing sensitive private portfolios, the self-hosted deployment must include a restrictive robots.txt file at the root directory 19:

User-agent: \*  
Disallow: /

#### **4.3 Task Scheduling and Cron Systems**

* The platform includes a background task scheduler (similar to DomainMOD's cron.php worker) that runs every 10 minutes.19 This worker processes scheduled queue items, calculates upcoming domain expirations, updates currency exchange rates, and sends local alert notifications.19
